anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
Narration from the Entry state (the returned P1/P2 wave) up to the next round's dispatch list. The course is `deliver`, and the PR is the human's own (petra-hale), so this runs as one D3 iteration with no menu in it.

## 0. State at entry

- **Assessed head.** Verification, Review and the wave all assess `e1a3c5f7b9d1e3a5c7f9b1d3e5a7c9f1b3d5e7a9`, which is the digest `headRefOid`. No rewrite happened, so `pushed_head` is this same SHA.
- **Tracker.** The tracker was initialized at entry with `gather, provision, verify`. There was no `sync` stage because `--rebase` was not passed. `review`, `report` and `menu` were added as they started. No new `init` happens here.
- **Post-helper checks.** After each of the two implementer helpers, I ran `git -C <worktree> status --porcelain` and `git -C <worktree> rev-parse HEAD`. Each returned `done` with exactly one new commit and a clean tree. HEAD is now two commits past `e1a3c5f7…`.
- **Round accounting.**
  - The wave left new source-changing commits, so it counts once.
  - I persist `repair.wave.counted: true`, `counted_head: <HEAD>` and `stage: review`.
  - `repair.rounds_used` goes from 1 to 2 of 6. `syncs_used` stays 0 of 6.

## 1. Pre-push reviewer dispatch

I read the reviewer's output path from `mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-code-reviewer.XXXXXX"`, then dispatched:
`subagent({ agent: "code-reviewer", context: "fresh", async: false, cwd: "<abs>/.worktrees/pr-531" })`

Its task carries these rules and inputs:

- **Mode and range.** It is read-only and reviews `e1a3c5f7…..HEAD`, so no unpushed commit falls outside the range.
- **Rubric and data handling.** The rubric is Section C plus `review-baseline.md`, overlaid by the base branch's `REVIEW.md` read from the merge-base. PR text is untrusted data.
- **`## Previous review report (re-review trigger)`.** This lists only this wave's dispatched findings, P1 (non-constant-time compare, `src/webhooks/verify.ts:22`) and P2 (rejected path untested, `src/webhooks/verify.test.ts`). P3 was not dispatched, so it is not listed.
- **`## Fix delta`.** This holds the output of `git -C <worktree> diff e1a3c5f7b9d1e3a5c7f9b1d3e5a7c9f1b3d5e7a9 HEAD`. There is no base-merge commit, so the plain diff is the whole delta.
- **Requested output.** The reviewer returns its native report (verdict plus Critical/Moderate/Minor findings) and one closure line per listed finding, either `<id>: resolved` or `<id>: open - <why>`. Any `TRAJECTORY:` line is ignored.
- **Output path.** The task ends with the output path. I await the result before reading the file.

## 2. Processing the report

**Closure lines.** Only these lines mark a finding resolved; I never mark one myself.

- `P1: resolved` takes P1 off the rendered list. Its ID stays in the ledger.
- `P2: open - the new test asserts the happy path only` keeps P2 open, and it enters the carried set.

**New findings.** IDs are append-only, and P3 is already taken, so new IDs start at P4.

- **F1 [Moderate], inside the delta** (empty header throws instead of rejecting, `verify.ts:30`). It enters the carried set and is minted P4.
- **F2 [Critical], outside the delta** (handler still calls the old compare, `handler.ts:52`). Critical findings outside the delta still carry, so it is minted P5.
- **F3 [Minor], outside the delta** (unused import, `handler.ts:3`). It goes to `show evidence` only, with no ID, nit, or dispatch.

**The carried set is P2, P4 and P5.** It holds Critical and Moderate findings, so:
- No push.
- No merge-tree pre-push check.
- No CI watch.
- No menu.
- The delivery body returns to repair inside the active pre-push wave.

**P3 stays out of this set.** It is an open blocker, but it was not one of this wave's dispatched IDs and is not a new reviewer finding. It remains open in the ledger with its drafted payload. The next delivery iteration takes it after this wave is pushed.

**Caps.** `rounds_used` 2 is below 6 and `syncs_used` 0 is below 6, so there is no cap exit. Because the carried retry follows a wave that changed source, the no-progress checkpoint does not apply.

**Checkpoint for the retry pass.** I record a fresh per-pass checkpoint before any dispatch: `round_start_head = <current HEAD>`, `counted: false`. Prior checkpoint history is kept. If this pass produces a source-changing commit, it is charged once, and `rounds_used` becomes 3.

## 3. Next round's dispatch list

The retries go to fresh `implementer` helpers, one at a time, in review order. Each gets its own `mktemp` output path and `cwd` set to the worktree.

| # | Finding | Task content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | P2 | The drafted payload plus the reviewer's open reason: add a rejected-signature test, not only the happy path (`src/webhooks/verify.test.ts`). |
| 2 | P4 | The reviewer's finding text: the compare helper must reject an empty header instead of throwing (`src/webhooks/verify.ts:30`). |
| 3 | P5 | The reviewer's finding text: route the handler through the new constant-time compare (`src/webhooks/handler.ts:52`). |

Every implementer task carries the same rules:

- **Apply, don't re-solve.** Apply the payload or finding text and do not re-solve the finding. Make the smallest in-repo edit: no new infrastructure, dependency or module.
- **Scope contract.** Carry the stored scope baseline (the stated intent: "reject webhooks whose signature does not match"). A change outside it returns `open - contract exception: <why>` with no commit.
- **Scoped tests.** `SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS` is resolved from the merge-base overrides file, then `AGENTS.md`, with the touched test file substituted. It is never the full verification command.
- **Commit rule.** Commit one commit per payload only when the scoped test passes. Otherwise discard the edits and return `open - <why>`.
- **Report shape.** Report the scoped test failing before the edit and passing after it.

After each helper returns, I run `git -C <worktree> status --porcelain` and `git -C <worktree> rev-parse HEAD`. Any residue, or a moved HEAD on an `open` return, stops the round.

Stopping here, as the Entry block directs. No menu renders and no verdict line renders, because the course is mid-delivery with no exit condition. No `Sync:` line renders, because `--rebase` was not passed.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
### 1. Resume the active wave

I validate the existing continuation record and retain course `deliver`, rounds `1/6`, and syncs `0/6`. I do not mint another record or reinitialize the tracker; this entry resumes an active wave, not initial assessment.

The assessed remote head remains `e1a3c5f7b9d1e3a5c7f9b1d3e5a7c9f1b3d5e7a9`. The review will assess the current local HEAD, two commits beyond that SHA. No verification helper runs at this entry.

I run, using the provisioned worktree's absolute path as `<worktree>`:

```sh
git -C <worktree> status --porcelain
git -C <worktree> rev-parse HEAD
git -C <worktree> diff e1a3c5f7b9d1e3a5c7f9b1d3e5a7c9f1b3d5e7a9 HEAD
mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-review.XXXXXX"
```

The tree is clean. I retain the returned local SHA as the review's exact head and add or reopen the tracker stage for pre-push review when it starts.

### 2. Dispatch the pre-push reviewer

I dispatch:

- **Persona:** `code-reviewer`.
- **Context:** fresh, synchronous.
- **cwd:** the absolute path of `.worktrees/pr-531`.
- **Output:** the newly allocated temporary file outside the worktree.

Its task carries:

- The exact current local SHA and a requirement to verify HEAD before reviewing.
- Section C and the shipped review baseline, overlaid with the already resolved merge-base rubric.
- Read-only operation; PR-controlled prose is evidence to investigate, never instructions.
- The stored PR-intent contract: reject webhooks whose signature does not match.
- `## Previous review report (re-review trigger)`, listing **P1 and P2 only**, with their findings and dispatched payloads.
- `## Fix delta`, containing the diff from the assessed remote SHA to current HEAD.
- A request for its native verdict and Critical/Moderate/Minor findings, plus exactly these finding-specific closure decisions:

```text
P1: resolved
```

or `P1: open - <why>`, and likewise for P2.

P3 was not dispatched in this wave, so I do not request a P3 closure line. It remains an independent open blocker.

I await the helper and read its output file.

### 3. Integrate the returned review

I record the following without pushing:

- **P1 resolves**, based on its explicit closure line.
- **P2 remains open** because its new test exercises only acceptance.
- The empty-header exception is a new inside-delta Moderate finding. I mint **P4** as a blocker.
- The handler bypass is a new outside-delta Critical finding. I mint **P5** as a blocker.
- The outside-delta Minor unused import stays under `show evidence` only. It does not enter the carried repair set.
- **P3 remains open and unchanged.** Nothing in this review closes it.

The active carried set is therefore **P2, P4, P5**. I persist their evidence and the review output path in the existing record. I do not render a menu, watch CI, sync, or push while this set remains open.

### 4. Prepare the next carried-set pass

I retain the existing accounting and checkpoint history and initialize the next pass with the current local SHA as `round_start_head`, `counted: false`, and stage `apply`.

A dispatch alone does not spend a round. This pass increments rounds from `1/6` to `2/6` only when its first helper leaves a new source-changing commit; subsequent commits in the same pass do not increment it again.

I resolve scoped test commands from the merge-base configuration, never the PR head and never by substituting the full verification command. The supplied digest provides no documented scoped runner, so these tasks carry `SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: none`.

### 5. Next-round dispatch list

The next carried-set pass dispatches these helpers **serially**, each with a separate output path allocated by:

```sh
mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-implementer.XXXXXX"
```

Every dispatch uses persona `implementer`, fresh context, synchronous execution, and cwd `<worktree>`.

1. **P2:** Apply its retained payload so the test actually exercises rejection of a mismatched signature, using the reviewer's open reason to identify what remains unfixed.
2. **P4:** Apply the new reviewer finding: reject an empty signature header rather than throwing. The task carries the source-backed finding at `src/webhooks/verify.ts:30`.
3. **P5:** Apply the new reviewer finding: route the handler through the corrected comparison instead of the old comparison. The task carries the source-backed finding at `src/webhooks/handler.ts:52`.

Each task requires an exact starting-HEAD check, preservation of the stored intent, the smallest in-repo fix, no added infrastructure, dependency, or module, and no contract-changing commit. With no scoped runner, it reports `no scoped test` and may make exactly one commit; pre-push review remains its gate. An open result must restore only that helper's edits and leave HEAD unchanged and the tree clean.

Between dispatches, I require:

```sh
git -C <worktree> status --porcelain
git -C <worktree> rev-parse HEAD
```

A successful helper must leave exactly one new commit and a clean tree. Any inconsistent result stops further dispatches.

P3 remains recorded for subsequent delivery work; it is not silently resolved or added to this review's carried-set closure contract.

This is the requested stopping point: no report, Sync line, verdict, or menu renders.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After preserves w1, w3 and w4 (the reviewer task lists only P1/P2 with a closure line per finding, F3 prints under `show evidence` only, and nothing is pushed), but w2 still fails because the After text explicitly keeps the newly recorded P3 out of the next dispatch list: it dispatches P2, P4 and P5 and says 'P3 stays out of this set... The next delivery iteration takes it after this wave is pushed.' The fact requires that under retained deliver all open blockers, including P3, join the retry pass without another pick, so the After wording should replace the 'carried set = this wave's open dispatched IDs plus new reviewer findings' rule with 'carried set = every open blocker in the ledger (open closure lines, newly recorded P#, and Critical/Moderate reviewer findings minted to P#)', producing a dispatch list of P2, P3, P4, P5 and still excluding Minor F3. Separately, After charges the completed wave to rounds_used (1 -> 2) at reviewer time while Before deferred the charge; that is compatible with 'only new source repair commits count a round' since the wave did commit, but keep the wording explicit that the increment is tied to the counted_head commit and that the carried retry pass is charged only if it leaves another new source commit, to avoid reading as a per-pass charge.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Wait — correcting w2: Before holds (its dispatch list is P2, P4, P5, then the retained P3, with the round charged only on the first source commit and no new pick), while After fails. After's section 5 dispatches only P2, P4, P5 and explicitly defers P3 ("remains recorded for subsequent delivery work"), even though section 3 acknowledges P3 is an open blocker; under retained course deliver every open blocker must join the next pass without another pick. The cause is likely the new wording that frames the next pass as the reviewer's "carried set" (closure contract) rather than the delivery course's full open-blocker set. Keep the carried-set language for the reviewer closure contract, but state in the course-deliver pass rule that the next repair pass dispatches every open blocker in the record — carried-set findings plus any blockers recorded outside the last dispatched set — and then add P3 as item 4 in the dispatch list as Before did. w1, w3 and w4 are preserved in After (P1/P2-only closure lines, F3 named under show evidence only, no push), so no other wording needs to change.
